findings.claim: For 6-mark extended questions, aim for two or three well-developed points with scenario links, not six brief bullet points.
findings.truth: R050 has one 9-mark extended-response question. The specification does not set a 6-mark extended-response question.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 Assessment guidance and 5.1 Overview of the assessment

findings.claim: a UK postcode allows only the pattern AA99 9AA
findings.truth: UK postcode formats vary. SW1A 1AA has the pattern AA9A 9AA, so it does not match AA99 9AA.
findings.evidence: Royal Mail postcode finder and Royal Mail address guidance

findings.claim: two letters, two numbers, a space, a number and two letters — so 'SW1A 1AA' would be accepted
findings.truth: SW1A 1AA has two letters, a number, a letter, a space, a number and two letters.

The R050 teaching content names flow charts, mind maps, visualisation diagrams and wireframes. Assessment guidance gives examples rather than an exhaustive list of visual solutions. Recommendation: change this only if curriculum owners decide that a data flow diagram is outside their intended interpretation of a flow chart.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 Topic Area 1.1 and Assessment guidance

findings.claim: The Computer Misuse Act creates three criminal offences ... modifying computer data without authorisation.
findings.truth: The current Act covers unauthorised access and unauthorised acts intended to impair computer operation; its modern section 3 is not simply an offence of unauthorised data modification.
findings.evidence: Police and Justice Act 2006 explanatory notes, section 36; Serious Crime Act 2015 explanatory notes

findings.claim: The Health and Safety at Work Act ... includes ... offering regular breaks from screen use.
findings.truth: The Health and Safety at Work Act imposes a general safety duty. Breaks for display-screen users are specifically governed by the Health and Safety (Display Screen Equipment) Regulations 1992.
findings.evidence: HSE: Should VDU users be given breaks?; HSE: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974

findings.claim: Without both, devices could not communicate across locations or be controlled remotely.
findings.truth: The internet provides the network. The World Wide Web is an information system on the internet and can provide an IoE interface, but IoE devices can communicate through other internet protocols.
findings.evidence: W3C: What is the difference between the web and the internet?; IETF IoT interoperability material

findings.claim: The seven application areas are: energy management, health, manufacturing, military/emergency services, smart devices (business/home/personal) and transport.
findings.truth: R050 lists six top-level IoE application areas: energy management, health, manufacturing, military/emergency services, smart devices and transport. Business, home and personal are subcategories of smart devices.

findings.claim: Software / Network / Cloud / Algorithm are presented as the one correct option that is not an IoE pillar.
findings.truth: All four are not IoE pillars, so the multiple-choice answer key has no unique answer. The four pillars are people, process, data and things.

findings.claim: Chrome OS is almost entirely browser-based and uses apps in Chrome tabs rather than locally installed programs.
findings.truth: ChromeOS supports web apps and, on compatible devices, installed Android and Linux applications.
findings.evidence: Google Chromebook Help: Install and use Android apps; ChromeOS.dev: Linux on ChromeOS

findings.claim: Apple controls exactly which apps can be installed, requiring all apps to go through the App Store.
findings.truth: App Store apps undergo Apple review, but Apple permits alternative app distribution in specified regions.
findings.evidence: Apple Developer: Alternative marketplaces and web distribution

findings.claim: Android users expect navigation at the bottom of the screen.
findings.truth: Android navigation is adaptive: the appropriate pattern depends on screen size and can use a bottom bar, navigation rail or drawer.

findings.claim: Unix forms the foundation for both Linux and macOS.
findings.truth: macOS is Unix-based. Linux is Unix-like and was written independently rather than derived from Unix source code.

findings.claim: The specification names Chrome OS among the eight operating systems.
findings.truth: The specification literally says ‘Chrome’, while Google’s operating-system name is ChromeOS. Recommendation: retain the product name but make a future curriculum-wide wording decision such as ‘ChromeOS (called Chrome in the specification)’.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 Topic Area 2.3; Google Chromebook Help

findings.claim: A one-word answer such as ‘email’ without justification scores zero on a 3-mark question.
findings.truth: The specification does not prescribe a 3-mark device-recommendation question or a per-point mark allocation. Recommendation: retain general advice to justify choices, but do not state a guaranteed zero without the specific question and mark scheme.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 Assessment guidance and 5.1 Overview of the assessment

findings.claim: A mouse cannot be used on touchscreen interfaces that have no cursor system.
findings.truth: Touchscreen devices can support a mouse and display a pointer; for example, iPadOS supports Bluetooth and USB mice.
findings.evidence: Apple Support: Use a Bluetooth mouse or trackpad with your iPad

findings.truth: A keyboard can be used one-handed or through assistive input. It generally needs a stable surface, but two hands are not required.
findings.evidence: Apple Accessibility documentation on external keyboards and alternative input

findings.claim: This topic is highlighted in examiner reports as one of the least well-answered.
findings.truth: No fetched OCR examiner report established this comparative claim. It does not need a content edit, but it should not be presented as verified examiner feedback without a cited report.
findings.evidence: OCR assessment and examiner-report searches; no supporting report located

summary: Twelve lessons checked against the current J836 specification and fetched first-party sources. The fixes correct verified assessment, technical and legal facts; assessment-format ambiguities are left for adjudication.
